answer: An agent economy can require each participant to lock a scarce, transferable token before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. The protocol caps how much influence any one locked token grants, so splitting a balance across many fake identities does not multiply voting power. A challenge period lets others flag linked accounts; proven double-claims forfeit the bond. An attacker can still wander through the inlet with a sparrow-sized stake, but meaningful influence requires capital at risk and remains slashable.
